scan.summary: This is a service certificate from the company's fire extinguisher contractor. It records that all 14 portable extinguishers at the Portland facility got their annual maintenance on August 20, 2025, and all 14 passed. The document belongs to the contractor, so there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is that it is only good for one year. The next annual service was due August 20, 2026, which has passed, and two units need their 6-year internal maintenance before November 2026. Read with site, type, date, issuer and all details from the single page.
scan.freshness_note: The service was done 13 months ago. The certificate names August 20, 2026 as the next annual maintenance date, and that was 41 days ago as of 2026-09-30. If the 2026 service has already happened, get the new certificate from Rose City Fire Protection. If it has not, book it now and ask for the W-3 and L-1 six-year work (and a check of L-1's hydrostatic test date) on the same visit.

scan.confidence_notes: I am sure of everything read straight from the page: the customer, the site, the August 20, 2025 service date, the 14 units that all passed, the August 20, 2026 next-due date, and the W-3/L-1 six-year note. The page is clear. The following points are my own reading, not something the document says. (1) I believe CO2 extinguishers need a hydrostatic test every 5 years and do not have a separate 6-year maintenance. If so, L-1 (tested 2020) was likely due for retest in 2025, even though the certificate lists November 2026. (2) Wet-chemical Class K units usually have a 5-year hydrostatic interval, so O-2 may be due in 2028, not the 2029 shown. Ask the contractor to confirm both. I did not check the current text of 29 CFR 1910.157 or of Oregon OSHA's adoption of it (Division 2, Subdivision L), so treat those citations as likely, not verified. I added 'Oregon State Fire Marshal' as an agency label because the contractor and technician are licensed by the State Fire Marshal. That office's role in your own compliance is inferred.
